title: Unravel decision serializer and trim legacy policy shims
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the smart routing decision serialization and remove legacy policy shims that add CPU overhead and complicated fallback semantics. The current decision path serializes a large routing context blob, runs it through multiple adapter layers (legacy combinators, policy shims, and a fallback translator), and then deserializes into per-region runtime structs. This creates allocation churn, duplicated validation logic, and several subtle inconsistency bugs when regional policy overrides are present. Goals: 1) Introduce a compact, forward-compatible DecisionPayload that eliminates repeated field copies; 2) Remove the legacy policy-shim layer and migrate consumers to the simplified policy-runtime interface; 3) Upgrade policy-engine-go dependency to 2.4.0 and protobuf definitions to the stable schema; 4) Add microbenchmarks and live canary to validate latency and fallback-rate improvements.
acceptance_criteria: New DecisionPayload used by router hotpath with max serialized size reduced by >=40% on typical requests
Request p95 routing latency reduced by >=10% under baseline workload in perf harness
Fallback invocation rate to legacy regional fallback logic reduced to zero for migrated routes
All existing integration tests pass and new tests cover edge cases for regional-policy overrides
Policy-engine-go dependency updated to v2.4.0 and protobuf compatibility tests added
Migration plan documented and rollout gated behind feature flag with automated rollback path
steps: Inventory shimmed adapters and list of routes that still depend on legacy combinator behavior
Design compact DecisionPayload and backwards-compatible translation layer
Implement DecisionPayload serializer/deserializer with zero-copy where possible
Add unit/microbench harness and measure allocations and CPU across path variants
Upgrade policy-engine-go to v2.4.0; run protobuf compatibility checks
Create migration CLI tool to validate route compatibility and emit migration report
Roll out behind feature flag: internal canary -> customer canary -> full rollout
Monitor conservatively for errors, fallback rate, and latency regressions; iterate
notes: This ticket addresses long-standing allocation spikes in the router hotpath seen in nightly perf runs. The compact DecisionPayload is intentionally conservative: it keeps region-level overrides inline but moves large metadata blobs to a lazy reference map. The migration CLI produces a per-route compatibility score. If score < 0.8 we will not auto-migrate and will file a follow-up ticket for manual review.
